children: said on Thursday it expected to report a net loss for 2026 due to higher than expected financial expenses, transformation costs and the impact of underperforming assets.
The company, which had previously expected to post a profit this year, also suspended its target for a positive net result in 2027 and 2028 dividend payment.
Voltalia, however, reiterated 2026 capacity and core profit objectives.
Talks are underway to exit or dispose of two more national markets under its transformation plan.
Voltalia now targets a footprint of around 12 geographies.
First-half EBITDA rose 30% at constant exchange rates to €110.3 million ($127.9 million).
Net loss widened to €43.3 million in the period, against a loss of €39.7 million a year ago.
